prompt: In the 3M unit, how does the text split the science and the art of fish farming?

options.text: The science is the technical know-how, and the art is the business
The science is the business, and the art is the technical know-how
Both refer to the same technical skills
The science is breeding, and the art is harvesting

explanation: Science equals technical know-how; art equals business. That split then maps onto the 3M: MAKE is the science, MANAGE and MULTIPLY are the art.

why.a: Correct. The text puts technical know-how with science and business with art.
why.b: Wrong. This reverses the two.
why.c: Wrong. The whole point of the phrase is that they are different.
why.d: Wrong. Breeding and harvesting are both technical activities.

prompt: Fish farming is the science, that is the technical know-how, and the art, that is the {{1}}, of rearing fish.
explanation: Business. Test 2 asked the same word about agripreneurship as a whole, where it is bringing a business mindset to agriculture.

prompt: Which of the following is listed as one of the "3Ms" of creating wealth in fish farming?

options.text: Make
Movement
Money
Market

explanation: Test 1, question 19, quoted as printed. The 3M are Make, Manage and Multiply. Only Make is offered here, and the other three options are near misses starting with the same letter.

why.a: Correct. Make is the first of the three Ms.
why.b: Wrong. Movement is not part of the model; slow movement is a behaviour category.
why.c: Wrong. Money is what the model produces, not one of its three names.
why.d: Wrong. Market is a MAKE principle and a marketing topic, but not one of the three Ms.

prompt: The 3M of creating wealth in fish farming is Make, Manage and {{1}}.
explanation: Multiply. Make, Manage, Multiply, in that order: build it, hold on to it, then grow it into several streams.

prompt: Which parts of the 3M model are the art, and which is the science?

options.text: Make is the science; Manage and Multiply are the art
Make and Manage are the science; Multiply is the art
Multiply is the science; Make and Manage are the art
All three are the science

explanation: One science, two arts. MAKE is the technical foundation, and everything after it is business.

why.a: Correct. The text says the Make is the science, while the Manage and Multiply are the art.
why.b: Wrong. Manage is business, so it belongs to the art.
why.c: Wrong. This inverts the model entirely.
why.d: Wrong. The whole point is that two of the three are business.

prompt: In the 3M model, MAKE is the science and foundation of fish farming.
explanation: MAKE carries the ten principles, and the text calls them the foundation, working interdependently like the fingers of your hand.

why.true: Correct. MAKE is described as the science and foundation of fish farming.
why.false: Wrong. The text names MAKE as the science; the art is Manage and Multiply.

prompt: Which elements belong to the MAKE component of the fish-farming wealth-creation framework?

options.text: Location, construction, feed, water, land, technical know-how and security.
Marketing mix, leverage, research, SWOT analysis and an integrated approach.
Car wash, restaurant, hairdressing salon, boutique, cybercafé and children's play centre.
Policies, regulations, discipline, training, internal controls and corporate monitoring.

explanation: Test 2, question 28, quoted as printed and confirmed correct on the graded paper. Every item in option A is one of the ten MAKE principles. Option B is MULTIPLY, option D is the human resources part of MANAGE, and option C is a list of unrelated small businesses.

why.a: Correct. Location, construction, feed, water, land, fisheries knowledge and manpower, and security are all MAKE principles.
why.b: Wrong. Marketing mix, leverage, research and the integrated approach all belong to MULTIPLY.
why.c: Wrong. These are ordinary small businesses with no place in the model.
why.d: Wrong. Policies, regulations, discipline and training are the effective human resources management item under MANAGE.

prompt: MAKE has {{1}} principles that should be religiously adhered to for a successful fish farm.
explanation: Ten, described as working interdependently like the fingers of your hand. Five is the number of MANAGE elements and six the number of MULTIPLY tasks.

prompt: What does the MAKE principle of water require?

options.text: The standard quality and quantity of water required for the fish to grow well
Water from a municipal supply only
Crystal clear water, regardless of its chemistry
The largest possible volume, whatever its quality

explanation: Quality and quantity together. The thumb rule follows from this principle: do not venture in without knowing the quality of your water.

why.a: Correct. Both quality and quantity are named in the principle.
why.b: Wrong, and an absolute. Surface water and pre-treated well water are both discussed.
why.c: Wrong. The text warns that clear water is not necessarily safe.
why.d: Wrong. Quantity without quality is exactly the mistake the unit warns against.

prompt: Why does the MAKE principle treat land as a decisive factor?

options.text: It determines the nature of the soil, the types of ponds whether earthen or concrete, and water availability and quality
It determines the market price of fish in the area
It determines the species of fish that will breed
It determines the cost of feed ingredients

explanation: Soil, pond type, water. Land is the principle that quietly decides several of the others.

why.a: Correct. These three consequences are named under land.
why.b: Wrong. Price is a matter for the market principle and for market research.
why.c: Wrong. Species choice rests on market research and on knowing your fish.
why.d: Wrong. Feed cost belongs to the feed availability and quality principle.

prompt: Which three measures does the text give under the MAKE principle of security?

options.text: Fencing the fish farm, installing a CCTV camera, and hiring a security guard
Quarantining new fish, using probiotics, and testing the water
Insurance, diversification, and innovative practices
Code of conduct, policy, and discipline

explanation: Fence, camera, guard. Keep this apart from biosecurity, which is about disease rather than theft.

why.a: Correct. These three are the security measures named.
why.b: Wrong. Those are biosecurity and water quality measures.
why.c: Wrong. Those are risk management tools from Module One.
why.d: Wrong. Those belong to effective human resources management under MANAGE.

prompt: Where you site your fish farm may or may not {{1}} the success of your fish farm.
explanation: Mar. The illustration is a road that floods and cuts the farm off, against a location where the fish is in high demand at a high price with no rival competitors.

prompt: Which MAKE principle does the text call a major key to making wealth in fish farming?

options.text: Fisheries knowledge and manpower
Finance
Construction
Security

explanation: Fisheries knowledge and manpower, because sound knowledge in rearing, breeding and marketing is called an essential prerequisite for a bountiful harvest.

why.a: Correct. The text singles this one out as a major key.
why.b: Wrong. Finance is about budgeting before you start.
why.c: Wrong. Construction is about building ponds that do not fail.
why.d: Wrong. Security protects the investment but is not called the major key.

prompt: Sound knowledge in rearing, breeding and marketing is an essential prerequisite for a {{1}} harvest.
explanation: Bountiful. Test 2 rendered this principle as technical know-how in its list of MAKE elements.

prompt: Why does the source of supply of fingerlings or juveniles matter?

options.text: The genetic composition of the parental stock determines the growth of the fingerlings and juveniles
The distance to the supplier determines the market price
The colour of the fingerlings determines their species
The supplier chooses the feed the farm must use

explanation: Genetics of the parent stock. It is the fish farming version of the oil palm point that Dura crossed with Pisifera gives the high-yielding Tenera.

why.a: Correct. Parental genetics determine how the young fish grow.
why.b: Wrong. Distance affects transport, not the stated reason here.
why.c: Wrong. Colour is not discussed as a species indicator for fish.
why.d: Wrong. Feed choice belongs to the feed availability and quality principle.

prompt: Locating the farm near the {{1}} market, where high-quality feed ingredients are sold all year round, adds to the farm's sustainability.
explanation: Agricultural market. Feed is 60 to 70 per cent of production cost, so proximity to good ingredients is a real economic factor.

prompt: What does the MAKE principle of market say your market research must find out?

options.text: Who your customers are, the price of fish, and who your competitors are
The pH and dissolved oxygen of the water source
The genetic composition of the parent stock
The thickness of the aquarium glass

explanation: Customers, price, competitors. The marketing unit later expands this into identifying the target market as the first step.

why.a: Correct. These three are named under the market principle.
why.b: Wrong. That is the water principle and the water quality section.
why.c: Wrong. That belongs to the source of fingerlings principle.
why.d: Wrong. Glass thickness is an aquarium setup step.

prompt: What does the text warn about badly constructed ponds?

options.text: They can be flooded or have broken walls, releasing fish that are stolen or die in the process
They raise the pH of the water permanently
They attract tourists who damage the farm
They reduce the shelf life of processed fish

explanation: Flooding and broken walls, and the fish lost either way. The instruction that follows is to seek professionals rather than patronising quacks.

why.a: Correct. Flooding, broken walls, and fish stolen or dying is the stated risk.
why.b: Wrong. pH is a chemical parameter unrelated to pond construction here.
why.c: Wrong. Agro-tourism is presented as an opportunity, not a hazard.
why.d: Wrong. Shelf life is a processing and storage matter.

prompt: Seek professionals to help you construct fishponds instead of patronising {{1}}.
explanation: Quacks. It is the text's own word, and phrasings this distinctive are what a wording question is built on.

prompt: What does the MAKE principle of finance instruct?

options.text: Create a budget for farm expenditure before you start, and rear the quantity of fish your budget can take care of
Borrow as much as possible to stock the largest number of fish
Avoid keeping any financial records
Spend the entire budget in the first month

explanation: Budget first, then stock to the budget. Financial prudence under MANAGE adds the other half: having a budget does not mean spending all of it.

why.a: Correct. Budget before starting, and stock what the budget can carry.
why.b: Wrong. Overstocking beyond your means contradicts the principle.
why.c: Wrong. Keeping records is the first MANAGE element.
why.d: Wrong. Financial prudence explicitly says otherwise.

prompt: Which of these is one of the five MANAGE elements?

options.text: Financial prudence
Technological input
Construction
Reward mechanism

explanation: The five are keeping records, financial prudence, communication skills, diligence and effective human resources management. Technological input and reward mechanism are MULTIPLY; construction is MAKE.

why.a: Correct. Financial prudence is the second MANAGE element.
why.b: Wrong. Technological input is the first MULTIPLY task.
why.c: Wrong. Construction is a MAKE principle.
why.d: Wrong. Reward mechanism is a MULTIPLY task.

prompt: MANAGE is set out with {{1}} elements, from keeping records to effective human resources management.
explanation: Five. Ten belongs to MAKE and six to MULTIPLY, so the three counts are 10, 5 and 6.

prompt: What does keeping records give the farmer, according to the MANAGE element?

options.text: A road map on whether the farm is making a profit or a loss
Immunity from taxation
A guarantee of loan approval
A way to avoid water testing

explanation: A road map on profit or loss, by monitoring expenditure and revenue. Record keeping returns in Module Four as farm management software.

why.a: Correct. Monitoring expenditure and revenue gives a road map on profit or loss.
why.b: Wrong. Nothing about taxation is claimed.
why.c: Wrong. No loan guarantee is offered anywhere.
why.d: Wrong. Water testing is never optional in this course.

prompt: Which example does the text give for financial prudence?

options.text: Fixing a broken pipe yourself instead of paying a plumber, and taking trainees who pay you to learn
Buying the most expensive equipment available
Spending the whole budget as soon as it is approved
Borrowing against the next harvest

explanation: Do it yourself, and let trainees pay to learn instead of paying extra staff. The principle is that a budget is a ceiling, not a target.

why.a: Correct. Both examples are given under financial prudence.
why.b: Wrong. Prudence is about cutting cost, not maximising spend.
why.c: Wrong. The text says explicitly that having a budget does not mean spending it all.
why.d: Wrong. No borrowing example appears under this element.

prompt: The fact that you have a budget does not mean you have to {{1}} the whole amount.
explanation: Spend. Cost control returns in Module Four as a component of operations management, measuring cost per unit to minimise waste.

prompt: What does the MANAGE element on communication skills say about how you speak to employees?

options.text: The way you talk to them will either kill their interest in working for you or motivate them, so see them as assets and use polite words
Employees should be addressed only in writing
Firm and abusive language produces the best results
Communication is the responsibility of the administrative department alone

explanation: Kill their interest or motivate them. The text gives the polite words to use and the abusive ones to avoid, which is unusually concrete for a management point.

why.a: Correct. This is the element word for word, including seeing employees as assets.
why.b: Wrong. No such restriction appears.
why.c: Wrong. The text explicitly says to avoid abusive language.
why.d: Wrong, and an absolute. The element is addressed to the owner.

prompt: Where does the MANAGE element of diligence say discipline starts?

options.text: With the owner of the farm, whose diligence makes it easier to instil discipline in employees
With the newest employee
With the written code of conduct alone
With the customers

explanation: With you, the owner. The code of conduct comes under the next element, human resources management, and it works only if the owner already models it.

why.a: Correct. It starts with the owner, whose diligence makes discipline easier to instil.
why.b: Wrong. The text points at the owner, not the staff.
why.c: Wrong, and the word alone is misplaced; the code belongs to the next element.
why.d: Wrong. Customers appear under the reward mechanism, not here.

prompt: In the "Manage" phase of the wealth creation roadmap, which of the following is identified as a critical component of Effective Human Resources Management?

options.text: Securing the physical location and source of fingerlings
Conducting a SWOT and SMART analysis for innovation
Establishing a code of conduct, policy, regulation, and discipline
Implementing technological inputs and networking

explanation: Test 1, question 26, quoted as printed. Effective human resources management is defined by measures: code of conduct, policies, regulations, discipline, training, controls and promotion.

why.a: Wrong. Location and source of fingerlings are MAKE principles.
why.b: Wrong. SWOT and SMART belong to research and development under MULTIPLY.
why.c: Correct. Code of conduct, policy, regulation and discipline are the human resources measures.
why.d: Wrong. Technological input and networking are MULTIPLY tasks.

prompt: The human resources measures are a code of conduct, policies, regulations, discipline, training, controls and {{1}}.
explanation: Promotion. Seven measures in all, and promotion is the one at the end that candidates drop.

prompt: What is MULTIPLY, in the 3M model?

options.text: Engaging in multiple streams of sustainable revenue after making and managing the wealth
Increasing the number of fish in each pond
Doubling the size of the farm every year
Reinvesting all profit into feed

explanation: Multiple streams of sustainable revenue. It is the answer to the unitary fish farmer problem: one source of income is fragile.

why.a: Correct. Multiple streams of sustainable revenue, after making and managing.
why.b: Wrong. More fish per pond is overcrowding, a cause of stress.
why.c: Wrong. No growth rate is prescribed.
why.d: Wrong, and an absolute. Investment under MULTIPLY includes non-agricultural businesses.

prompt: MULTIPLY is set out with {{1}} tasks, from technological input to an integrated approach.
explanation: Six: technological input, leverage and networking, the marketing mix, investment, reward mechanism, and an integrated approach.

prompt: In the "3M" roadmap for wealth creation, the {{1}} phase is where a farmer focuses on technological input, networking, and the 7P's of the marketing mix to expand the business.
explanation: Test 1, question 9, quoted as printed. Technological input, networking and the 7Ps are three of the six MULTIPLY tasks, so naming any one of them points at Multiply.

prompt: Which technologies does the MULTIPLY task of technological input name?

options.text: Drones, AI sensors, automated feeders and apps
Air stones, filters and air pumps
Sand filters, activated carbon and iron-removal filters
Algae scrapers and magnetic cleaners

explanation: Drones, AI sensors, automated feeders, apps, all to increase productivity and harvest. The other options are aeration, iron removal and glass cleaning equipment.

why.a: Correct. These four are the technologies named under technological input.
why.b: Wrong. Those are aeration equipment, the remedy for slow movement.
why.c: Wrong. Those are iron removal filters from the water quality section.
why.d: Wrong. Those are weekly aquarium cleaning tools.

prompt: What example does the text give for leverage and networking?

options.text: Engaging a transportation company to use their bus to convey fish to customers
Buying a competitor's farm outright
Hiring more permanent staff
Building your own feed mill

explanation: Use someone else's bus. The principle stated is that no man is an island: what you do not have can be got from another company for mutual benefit.

why.a: Correct. The transport company example is the one the text gives.
why.b: Wrong. No acquisition example appears.
why.c: Wrong. Leverage is about using other companies rather than expanding your payroll.
why.d: Wrong. Building a feed mill is vertical integration, not leverage of another company.

prompt: The principle behind leverage and networking is that no man is an {{1}}.
explanation: Island. What you do not have can be got from another company for mutual benefit.

prompt: To achieve a complete "multiplying effect" in fish wealth creation, marketing strategies must integrate which specific frameworks?

options.text: The 7P's and 4C's of Marketing
The SMART and Value Addition metrics
The 3M's and SWOT Analysis
The USP and Hygiene Assurance protocols

explanation: Test 1, question 11, quoted as printed. The marketing pair inside MULTIPLY is the 7Ps and the 4Cs. SWOT and SMART are the research and development pair, and USP and hygiene belong to branding.

why.a: Correct. The 7Ps and the 4Cs are the two marketing frameworks under MULTIPLY.
why.b: Wrong. SMART is a diagnostic model, and value addition is a separate idea.
why.c: Wrong. The 3M is the whole model, and SWOT is a research tool.
why.d: Wrong. USP and hygiene and quality assurance are brand-building steps in the marketing unit.

prompt: In the 7Ps, physical evidence stands for {{1}}.
explanation: Packaging. The two glossed Ps are physical evidence, which is packaging, and process, which is positioning.

prompt: Which of these is NOT one of the 7Ps of the marketing mix?

options.text: Product
Price
Profit
People

explanation: The seven are product, promotion, place, price, physical evidence which is packaging, people, and process which is positioning. Profit is not among them.

why.a: Wrong as an answer. Product is the first P.
why.b: Wrong as an answer. Price is the fourth P.
why.c: Correct. Profit is not one of the 7Ps.
why.d: Wrong as an answer. People is the sixth P.

prompt: What are the 4Cs of marketing?

options.text: Customer, cost, convenience and communication
Cash, credit, capital and compliance
Colour, clarity, consistency and cleanliness
Crop, cattle, catfish and cassava

explanation: Customer, cost, convenience, communication. The text adds the reason: this is what you do when you put the customer first, because the customer is king.

why.a: Correct. These four are the 4Cs.
why.b: Wrong. None of these appears as a marketing C in the course.
why.c: Wrong. Colour and clarity are water quality parameters.
why.d: Wrong. These are commodities, not a marketing framework.

prompt: The 4Cs put the customers first in your decisions, because the customer is {{1}}.
explanation: King. It is the text's own phrasing and the reason the 4Cs sit beside the 7Ps rather than replacing them.

prompt: Under the MULTIPLY task of investment, where can profit from the fish farm be diversified?

options.text: Into other businesses like stocks and shares, which are not agriculturally based
Only into other fish farms
Only into feed production
Into land purchase exclusively

explanation: Stocks and shares, explicitly non-agricultural. It is the one place in the course that sends money outside farming altogether.

why.a: Correct. The text names stocks and shares as not agriculturally based.
why.b: Wrong, and an absolute. The point is diversification beyond the sector.
why.c: Wrong, and an absolute. Feed production is an investment opportunity, but not the answer here.
why.d: Wrong, and an absolute. Land is a MAKE principle, not the investment task.

prompt: Who is the reward mechanism for, and what form does it take?

options.text: Staff and customers, in the form of a rebate or special award and gifts
Staff only, in the form of a fixed bonus
Customers only, in the form of free fish
Suppliers, in the form of early payment

explanation: Staff and customers both, and the reason given is sincere loyalty. Loyalty programmes for customers appear again in the marketing unit.

why.a: Correct. Staff and customers, with rebates or special awards and gifts.
why.b: Wrong, and the word only cuts out customers.
why.c: Wrong, and the word only cuts out staff.
why.d: Wrong. Suppliers are not named in this task.

prompt: The integrated approach with agro-allied businesses is illustrated by the optimal utilisation of your generator and water {{1}}.
explanation: Water pumps. The idea is that equipment already paid for should earn its keep across more than one enterprise.

prompt: Which diagnostic models are identified for research and planning before starting or expanding an aquaculture venture?

options.text: PESTEL analysis and Porter's Five Forces.
SWOT analysis and SMART analysis.
The BCG Matrix and the Ansoff Matrix.
The Lean Canvas and the Balanced Scorecard.

explanation: Test 2, question 4, quoted as printed and confirmed correct on the graded paper. SWOT and SMART are the only two models named anywhere in this course; every other framework in the options is imported from outside it.

why.a: Wrong. Neither PESTEL nor Porter's Five Forces appears in the course.
why.b: Correct. SWOT analysis and SMART analysis head the research and development questions.
why.c: Wrong. Neither matrix appears in the course.
why.d: Wrong. Neither the Lean Canvas nor the Balanced Scorecard appears in the course.

prompt: The two research and development questions the text puts first are: have you done your {{1}} analysis, and have you done your S.M.A.R.T analysis?
explanation: SWOT. POCD is the operations management framework in Module Four, and USP belongs to branding, so keep the acronyms apart.

prompt: Besides SWOT and SMART, which question does the research and development list ask?

options.text: What innovation and creativity can distinguish my business?
How many fish can I fit into one pond?
Which bank offers the lowest interest rate?
How can I avoid keeping records?

explanation: Innovation and creativity as a differentiator. The list also asks what others have done, what has not been fully developed, how to make it happen, what the marketing strategies are, and what the packaging will look like.

why.a: Correct. This question is on the research and development list.
why.b: Wrong. Stocking density is a management matter, and overcrowding causes stress.
why.c: Wrong. No banking question appears on the list.
why.d: Wrong. Keeping records is a MANAGE element, not something to avoid.

prompt: Which strategic approach is most appropriate for building a resilient and profitable fish-farming enterprise?

options.text: Convert every farm exclusively to cage culture on public rivers.
Ignore marketing principles and rely only on open wholesale brokers.
Depend entirely on government subventions and remove staff reward mechanisms.
Be creative, maximise available resources, reduce unnecessary costs and increase productive output.

explanation: Test 2, question 11, quoted as printed and confirmed correct on the graded paper. It is the text's own conclusion to the 3M unit, set against the unitary fish farmer who has only one source of income.

why.a: Wrong. Every and exclusively are absolutes, and no such conversion is recommended.
why.b: Wrong. Only is an absolute, and the whole marketing unit argues the opposite.
why.c: Wrong. Entirely is an absolute, and the reward mechanism is a MULTIPLY task worth keeping.
why.d: Correct. Be creative, maximise resources, reduce cost and increase output.

prompt: A {{1}} fish farmer gets income from one source, but the best approach to a free-flowing income is to be creative.
explanation: Unitary. It is the word the text uses for a farmer with a single income stream, which is exactly what MULTIPLY exists to fix.

prompt: How does the in-text answer say production costs are reduced in fish farming?

options.text: By producing your own feed, using technology, and proper farm management that minimises waste, for example running fish, maize and poultry on one farm
By reducing the number of water changes
By buying the cheapest fingerlings regardless of parent stock
By skipping water quality tests

explanation: Own feed, technology, and integrated management. Producing your own feed attacks the largest cost, at 60 to 70 per cent of production.

why.a: Correct. These three, with the mixed farm as the example.
why.b: Wrong. Skipping water changes causes disease and losses.
why.c: Wrong. Parent stock genetics determine growth, so cheap stock costs more later.
why.d: Wrong. The thumb rule makes water testing non-negotiable.

prompt: What three things does market research identify, according to the in-text answer?

options.text: The most profitable fish species, the best-selling sizes, and the target buyers
The pH, the dissolved oxygen, and the turbidity
The pond type, the feed type, and the aeration rate
The staff, the training, and the code of conduct

explanation: Species, sizes, buyers. Understanding customer preferences is what lets you sell at the best price.

why.a: Correct. These three are named in the in-text answer on market research.
why.b: Wrong. Those are water quality parameters.
why.c: Wrong. Those are production decisions.
why.d: Wrong. Those belong to human resources management.

prompt: In the self-assessment answer on creating sustainable wealth, what does diversification mean for a fish farmer?

options.text: Smoked fish, fish fillets, integrated fish farming with crop farming, and integration with agro-allied businesses
Buying more ponds and stocking them with the same species
Selling only to one wholesale buyer
Switching entirely out of fish into poultry

explanation: Two processed products and two integrations. It is the practical version of MULTIPLY.

why.a: Correct. These four are the diversification routes named.
why.b: Wrong. More of the same is not diversification.
why.c: Wrong, and an absolute. A single buyer is the opposite of building market channels.
why.d: Wrong. Integration means adding, not switching.

prompt: Costs are reduced by converting waste like fish water {{1}} into organic fertiliser for crops or vegetables.
explanation: Effluents. It is the fish farming version of agricultural waste management, and the same idea as turning POME into biogas in Module Three.

prompt: Which three cost-reduction measures does the self-assessment answer name?

options.text: Automatic feeders, converting fish water effluents into organic fertiliser, and using interns to reduce manpower cost
Reducing aeration, feeding less, and skipping grading
Buying land, building more ponds, and hiring more guards
Raising prices, cutting delivery, and dropping packaging

explanation: Automatic feeders, effluent reuse, interns. Interns echo the financial prudence element, where trainees pay you to learn.

why.a: Correct. These three are the named cost reductions.
why.b: Wrong. Each of those would damage the stock.
why.c: Wrong. Those are capital expenditures, not cost reductions.
why.d: Wrong. Those are pricing and marketing decisions, and dropping packaging loses value.

prompt: What does the self-assessment answer say about learning and networking?

options.text: Attend fish farming workshops and training, join fish farming associations, and learn from other successful agripreneurs and from your own research
Keep your methods secret from all other farmers
Rely only on what you learned at the start
Avoid associations because they raise costs

explanation: Workshops, associations, learning from others. It is the same instinct as leverage and networking under MULTIPLY.

why.a: Correct. These three are named under keep learning and networking.
why.b: Wrong, and an absolute. The course encourages joining associations.
why.c: Wrong, and an absolute. Continuous learning is the point.
why.d: Wrong. Associations are recommended, including for market access.

prompt: Match each item to the phase of the 3M model it belongs to.

pairs.left: Code of conduct, policy and discipline

explanation: Both tests asked this sorting in one form or another. If you can place an item in its phase, you can answer nearly every 3M question on the paper.

prompt: MAKE is {{1}}, MANAGE is {{2}}, and MULTIPLY is {{3}}.

accept: the science and foundation, built on ten principles
choices: the science and foundation, built on ten principles
the art of holding on to money already earned
the art of building several streams of revenue
the process of selling fish at the highest possible price

accept: the art of keeping what has been made from reducing
choices: the art of keeping what has been made from reducing
the science of rearing fish to marketable size
the art of expanding into several income streams
the practice of testing water before stocking

accept: engaging in multiple streams of sustainable revenue
choices: engaging in multiple streams of sustainable revenue
constructing ponds that will not flood or break
keeping records of expenditure and revenue
feeding the fish to satiation to avoid cannibalism

explanation: Build it, hold it, grow it. Every question either test asked about the 3M is answered by knowing which of those three a given activity serves.
